anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: The submitted statements, transaction boundaries, or batching strategy are written in a way that forces the engine to touch more rows, transfer more bytes, or hold locks longer than the functional requirement dictates.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly: The transport layer between client and database cannot sustain the offered connection or data-transfer rate because of socket, listener, authentication, or physical network limitations.

When these two root causes manifest simultaneously, the database exhibits a super-position of engine-side latency and network-side latency. Over-wide scans, bulky result sets, and long-lived transactions generated by the logical workload flaw inflate the volume and duration of data that must traverse the network. At the same time, constrained connection slots, high round-trip time, handshake overhead, or packet loss delay the delivery of each oversized request and response. Operators may observe: a surge of identical slow-query log entries intertwined with client-read/client-write wait events; application timeouts during both connection establishment and statement execution; exponential growth of half-open sockets and idle backends stuck in network waits; elevated retransmission rates exactly when statement latency histograms show long tails; and connection pool exhaustion even though the server’s CPU and I/O metrics remain moderate.

Causally, the verbose SQL workload amplifies pressure on every stage of the network pipeline by demanding more result bytes per transaction and by holding sessions open longer, which in turn ties up limited connection slots and increases the backlog on the listener. Conversely, network congestion or authentication delays stretch each already-inefficient transaction, causing application retries that re-issue the same sub-optimal statements and further multiply load on the engine. The feedback loop between chatty or bloated SQL patterns and network resource scarcity deepens lock hold times, inflates memory used for result buffering, and starves new sessions, ultimately degrading overall throughput and making it difficult to isolate whether the primary bottleneck is intra-engine processing or inter-host transport.

entry.official_definition: Aborts any statement that waits longer than the specified amount of time while attempting to acquire a lock.
entry.trigger_condition: A statement waits longer than lock_timeout for a table, index, row, or other database object lock.
entry.workload_impact: The statement attempting to acquire the lock is aborted.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
